source.title: Reconciling Modern Deep Learning with Traditional Optimization Analyses: The Intrinsic Learning Rate
source.authors: Zhiyuan Li; Kaifeng Lyu; Sanjeev Arora

record.tranche_reason: The paper reports its own training and test performance under changes to learning-rate and weight-decay schedules, which bear on generalization conditions. It does not test the random-label, width, architecture, optimizer, batch-size, dropout, sharpness-measure, or memorized-example claims in the listed versions.
record.gate_note: Reports test/train accuracy and error under learning-rate and weight-decay schedules. The paper discusses batch-size effects but provides no experiment varying batch size. Figure-only curves are not used to infer precise values.
record.test_reason: The study tests learning-rate/weight-decay schedule equivalence and equilibrium in normalized networks, rather than any listed claim version. Batch size is explicitly held fixed; discussion of batch-size scaling and sharp minima does not establish V5 or V7. There are no adaptive-versus-SGD, dropout, architecture, width, random-label, or memorized-example-removal comparisons.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate. The authors develop an SDE framework for scale-invariant networks with normalization and weight decay, identify the learning-rate/weight-decay product as intrinsic learning rate, and report schedule-independent equilibrium performance and successful small-initial-learning-rate training given enough time. Fast function-space equilibration in inverse-intrinsic-learning-rate time remains an empirically motivated conjecture whose precise conditions are unresolved.
record.recipe_differences: Studies normalized networks with batch normalization and weight decay, varying learning-rate and weight-decay schedules; it does not reproduce a listed version's intervention or measure.
record.method_sensitivity: Learning-rate and weight-decay schedules and their product; initialization scale and schedule history also affect the reported convergence behavior.

fits_no_version.finding: Matching intrinsic learning rates yields similar train/test performance after equilibrium, including similar subsequent fine-tuning curves; the five CIFAR-10 PreResNet32 schedules reach approximately 95% best test accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In the tested scale-invariant normalized networks, equilibrium performance and subsequent fine-tuning can become insensitive to earlier schedules when the learning-rate/weight-decay product matches.

fits_no_version.finding: Small initial learning rates can attain comparable test performance with sufficiently long training, while recovery to equilibrium scales approximately inversely with intrinsic learning rate.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Large initial learning rates can accelerate training without being necessary for the final test performance of the tested normalized networks.

record.problems: The Fast Equilibrium Conjecture is presented as a conjecture, and the authors say its specific conditions remain future work. Several results are shown only in figures; the text gives no uncertainty intervals for the reported accuracy results. The experiments focus on scale-invariant networks with normalization and weight decay.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows extracted. The paper discusses prior batch-size and sharp-minima findings, but those are not its own results. Figure-only traces without a textual result were not split into separate schedule-specific rows.

untested.parts: Random-label memorization alongside natural-label generalization and chance-level random-label test accuracy.
Test-error changes with width beyond zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the role of local connectivity or initialization.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning, including weight-decay and switching remedies.
Large versus small batches under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations. The paper fixes batch size and explicitly limits its theoretical batch-size analogy.
Dropout benefits, small-data and excessive-dropout exceptions, and joint removal of dropout and weight decay with augmentation.
Magnitude-aware sharpness versus generalization gaps and comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: All row states are evaluated against the listed versions; cannot_determine with versions none does not dispute the study's reported schedule effects. High natural-label accuracy alone does not test V1, and removing weight decay during fine-tuning alone does not test V6.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Width sweeps beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparisons.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD or momentum, including the stated tuning and language-model conditions.
Large versus small batch sizes under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations to the training recipe.
Dropout and weight-decay effects in the stated regimes.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and comparisons with norm- or margin-based measures.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the effect on test accuracy.

rows.subject: simple 4-layer CNN
rows.operation_detail: Compared Const, LR-decay, and WD-decay schedules; all shared the same intrinsic learning rate from epoch 81 to 120.
rows.note: The authors report that schedules with matching intrinsic learning rates reached nearly the same train/test errors in this interval.
rows.check: The reported schedule equivalence is supported, but it measures no listed version. Its observed state cannot be interpreted as observing one of those versions.

rows.subject: simple 4-layer CNN
rows.operation_detail: Fine-tuned after setting learning rate to 0.01 and weight decay to 0 at epoch 121.
rows.value: all schedules show the same curve of decreasing train/test errors
rows.note: The text explicitly describes matching fine-tuning curves across the schedules.
rows.check: Matching fine-tuning curves after jointly changing learning rate and weight decay do not test V6's dropout interventions or joint removal of dropout and weight decay.

rows.subject: PreResNet32
rows.operation_detail: Compared five random learning-rate/weight-decay schedules, then set learning rate and weight decay the same at epoch 500 and removed weight decay after epoch 1000.

conditions.value: same LR and WD at 500; WD removed at 1000

rows.measure: Train/test accuracy and best test accuracy
rows.value: trajectories exhibit similar test/train accuracy; same best test accuracy (∼ 95%) after decaying LR and removing WD
rows.note: Figure caption reports aggregate similarity across the five schedules; exact individual schedule values are not stated.
rows.check: The approximately 95% best test accuracy and similarity across schedules are supported. This is a schedule comparison within SGD, not an adaptive-optimizer comparison or another listed intervention.

rows.subject: PreResNet32
rows.operation_detail: Used momentum SGD with an initially smaller learning rate and compared with the baseline schedule.

conditions.value: small initial learning-rate schedule versus baseline

rows.note: The caption says the small-learning-rate run achieved SOTA test accuracy, but supplies no precise value or textual comparison value.
rows.check: The text explicitly reports comparable performance from small initial learning rates after longer training, so the qualitative comparison is available even without precise figure values. It nevertheless bears on no listed version. Figure 3's small initial learning rate is 0.001, with a further decay at epoch 5000.

rows.subject: VGG16
rows.operation_detail: Compared different intrinsic learning rates, then changed learning rate and weight decay while maintaining their product.

conditions.value: different values; product maintained during the subsequent change

rows.measure: Train/test accuracy and steps to reach equilibrium
rows.value: text reports number of steps to reach equilibrium scales inversely with intrinsic LR; accuracy values figure only
rows.note: The stated result concerns equilibrium time; the figure shows accuracy curves without a stated textual accuracy comparison.
rows.check: The inverse relationship between intrinsic learning rate and recovery time is explicitly reported. Neither equilibrium time nor weight-norm convergence measures V7's magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance or its correlation with generalization gaps.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
